item: owner closure item 2 — resolve the verified export-vs-committed bundle drift
ownerRuling: the two independent live exports are authoritative because they are byte-identical to each other; commit one verified export's posts.json and manifest.json; change no semantic count, classification, span, id or post value

manifestJson.derivation: totalBytes = size(public/data/posts.json) + the five non-posts collections (1,940,184)
manifestJson.whyTheCommittedValueWasWrong: 11892314 - 1940184 = 9952130, but the committed posts.json is 10400163 bytes; the manifest described a bundle that is not the one beside it
manifestJson.method: the single field was rewritten in place and the resulting file hashed; it matches the value two independent live exports recorded, so these are the export's bytes rather than a retyped figure

postsJson.status: DEFERRED BY OWNER RULING to the deploy's own export
postsJson.why: its export-path bytes were deleted with the Gate 2 worktrees, as that gate's cleanup step required, and no live export may be spent here
postsJson.reconstructionResult: rejected — a deterministic rebuild of the committed documents came out 10,381,020 bytes against the required 10,400,163, so it could not be proven byte-identical to sha256 48544362d81763feac312cc1db285b002c25fdbb70c3870a875b8bc5299b70b1
postsJson.principle: a certified artifact is not committed from a reconstruction that cannot be proven

driftIsOrderOnly.where: the chain-appended claimMeta and directiveFamilies, and some nested postAnalysis key order

postsJson.quotaContext: Gate 2's two exports spent roughly 33,300 of the daily 50,000 reads; a third would cost about 16,600 and would leave nothing for the deploy that must run one anyway
postsJson.closedBy: the deploy export in the next quota window, whose posts.json is the authoritative source
